result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers define horizontal, stacked and mark-only versions, assign one to each placement, and treat the tote as a one-color screen print. A comes out slightly ahead because it builds a dedicated small-size redraw for the avatar that names exactly what to drop, and it adds a black-and-reversed check of whether the S still reads. B gives more concrete production specs, such as bleed, a 7 pt minimum, 1.5 mm gaps and a file handoff table, but it only simplifies the avatar mark if needed. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers define horizontal, stacked and mark-only versions, assign each to a placement, and are clearly organized by placement. B is slightly stronger: it specifies a dedicated small-size redraw for the avatar that thickens the gaps and drops spine detail. It also adds black-and-white and reversed checks that test how the mark holds up without color. A gives somewhat more concrete minimum sizes for the full lockup, but B's handling of the compact version and of the one-color print case is more thorough.
